summary: Iteration 12 (backend only, time-boxed): re-verified the 'stuck queued' fix. PASS: (1) First single approve creates exactly 1 pass job (v1, pending) with status 'queued'. The real worker then delivered it and the status became 'sent'. (2) Bulk-approve of 2 regs created 1 job each, queued -> sent (delivered 15:09 UTC). (3) Re-approving an already-sent reg returns 200 with pass_email_status 'sent', still 1 job (status sent), no new job. (4) resend-email on a sent job set that job back to pending (attempts 0) and the status to 'queued', still 1 job. The worker then redelivered it (new sent_at) and the status went back to 'sent'. (5) The worker starts after the startup recovery: after 'supervisorctl restart backend', 'Application startup complete' was followed 2.5 s later by 'Email provider busy; pausing 60s' for a pending job, so jobs keep being processed. (6) Regression test_iter11_email_queue.py passed 5/5. New test_iter12_reapprove_resend_status.py passed 4/4. One new minor edge case was found (below).

minor.issue: The resend update_many re-queues every 'pass' job for the registration, whatever its key. After reject (pass revoked) -> re-approve (pass v2), there are v1 and v2 jobs. Resend then sets BOTH back to pending, so the student gets 2 identical 'pass ready' emails and 2 provider sends are used. Reproduced: jobs after resend = [('v1','pending'),('v2','pending')]. Fix: limit the update to the current key, i.e. key = f"v{pass.version}" (the same key that _send_pass_email computes).

action_items: resend_pass_email (server.py:857): add the current pass key to the update_many filter so older-version jobs are not re-sent (look up db.passes version, key=f'v{version}').
critical_code_review_comments: _send_pass_email now maps an existing job's status to the registration status (sent/failed/skipped->failed, else queued). This is correct and fixes the iteration-11 bug.
Worker task is started at server.py:447, after the indexes are created and recovery runs. It is held in _bg_tasks, which prevents it from being garbage-collected. Good.

The queue is FIFO by created_at, so a reminder job that keeps getting 429 blocks the pass jobs behind it. Each retry pauses 60 s. With the preview provider limits, a newly approved student's pass email can wait several minutes behind bulk reminders. Consider giving 'pass' jobs priority over 'reminder' jobs (sort by kind, then created_at).

success_rate.backend: 100% of requested checks (iter12 4/4, iter11 regression 5/5, worker-after-restart verified); 1 new minor edge case

seed_data_creation: TEST Iter12 regs (@resend.dev, br-1) plus TEST Iter11 regs and a coordinator from the regression run. All cleaned up: 11 TEST* registrations, 11 passes and 22 email_queue jobs deleted, test_coord1x staff deleted, db.settings.deleteMany({}) run. The 5 real registrations were not touched, and the queue now holds only 4 'sent' jobs (real regs).
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini runs xdist with 2 workers (LoadScopeScheduling keeps each module on one worker). The iter12 test waits up to ITER12_WAIT_SENT (default 90 s) for real delivery. If the provider returns 429 it simulates the worker's 'sent' update in the DB, recorded under 'simulated' in /tmp/iter12_state.json. In this run delivery was real, nothing was simulated. Provider 429s are frequent, about 1 send per minute after a burst. Running test_iter11 queues reminders for all approved regs, including those from other tests.
rca_of_issue: Iteration-11 bug verified fixed: _send_pass_email no longer sets 'queued' unconditionally, and resend revives 'sent' jobs. New edge case: resend's update_many filter has no key, so jobs for older pass versions are revived as well.
